full_text_en:
Zibo Wanjie Hospital v. Bank of China Co., Ltd. Zibo Boshan Sub-branch, Zibo Boyi Fiber Co., Ltd., and Wanjie Group Co., Ltd. — objection to jurisdiction in a dispute over a loan guarantee contract

Ruling Summary

In interpreting contractual provisions, it is necessary to ascertain the intrinsic and true expression of intent of the parties to the contract. The primary method for determining the true expression of intent of the parties to a contract is to ascertain the literal expression of intent of the contractual provisions, i.e., the method of textual interpretation. Only when the precise meaning of a contractual provision cannot be determined through textual interpretation may other methods of interpretation be applied.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 99

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Zibo Wanjie Hospital, domiciled at Bashan Village, Boshan District, Zibo City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Qiyu, President of the Hospital.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Bank of China Co., Ltd. Zibo Boshan Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 63, Zhongxin Road, Boshan District, Zibo City, Shandong Province.
Responsible Person: Wang Rui, President of the Sub-branch.

Defendant at First Instance: Zibo Boyi Fiber Co., Ltd., domiciled at Bashan Village, Boshan District, Zibo City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Zheng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Wanjie Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Bashan Village, Boshan District, Zibo City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Qiyu, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The appellant, Zibo Wanjie Hospital (hereinafter referred to as Wanjie Hospital), appealed to this Court against the civil ruling (2007) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 17 of the Shandong High People's Court regarding the objection to jurisdiction in the dispute over the loan guarantee contract with the appellee, Bank of China Co., Ltd. Zibo Boshan Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch), the defendant at first instance, Zibo Boyi Fiber Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Boyi Company), and the defendant at first instance, Wanjie Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wanjie Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Presiding Judge Pei Yingshuo, Judge Zhu Hainian, and Acting Judge Gong Bangyou, to conduct the hearing. Court Clerk An Yang served as record keeper. This case is now concluded.

Upon review, the Shandong High People's Court found that: Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch and Wanjie Hospital, Boyi Company, and Wanjie Company entered into a total of nine loan contracts and corresponding guarantee contracts. Among them, the first loan contract, numbered Zi Zhong Bo Jie Zi No. 2004050, for the amount of USD 3,000,000, signed on October 14, 2004, stipulated in Article 17 regarding the application of law, dispute resolution, and jurisdiction: "This contract is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. Any disputes or controversies arising from the performance of this contract or related to this contract shall be settled through negotiation between the parties. If negotiation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the Zibo City Arbitration Commission for arbitration." The remaining eight loan contracts and corresponding guarantee contracts each stipulated: "This contract is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. Any disputes or controversies arising from the performance of this contract or related to this contract shall be settled through negotiation between the parties. If negotiation fails, the dispute shall be directly submitted to the People's Court at the location of the lender for litigation." The total loan amount covered by these eight contracts was USD 11,420,000, equivalent to RMB 89,175,354. Based on the above facts, the Shandong High People's Court held that, among the loan contracts sued upon by Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch, the arbitration clause in the first loan contract involving USD 3,000,000 was valid, and therefore the court had no jurisdiction over that matter. However, for the remaining eight loan contracts involving USD 11,420,000, there was no arbitration clause, and they stipulated direct submission to the People's Court at the location of the lender. Since the subject matter of the eight contracts was USD 11,420,000, equivalent to RMB 89,175,354, which exceeded the jurisdictional limit of the Boshan District People's Court in Zibo City where Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch was located, it fell within the scope of cases accepted by the Shandong High People's Court as approved by the Supreme People's Court. Therefore, accepting the case was not improper. In summary, among the nine loan contracts involved in this case, the objection to jurisdiction raised by Wanjie Hospital with respect to the loan contract numbered Zi Zhong Bo Jie Zi No. 2004050 for USD 3,000,000 was well-founded and was supported by the court; the objection to jurisdiction raised with respect to the remaining eight loan contracts lacked factual basis and was not supported. Pursuant to Article 38 and Article 111, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 5 of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 139 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. The action brought by Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch against Wanjie Hospital, Boyi Company, and Wanjie Group based on the loan contract numbered Zi Zhong Bo Jie Zi No. 2004050 for USD 3,000,000 signed on October 14, 2004, and the corresponding guarantee contract, was dismissed. 2. The objection to jurisdiction raised by Wanjie Hospital with respect to the remaining eight loan contracts in this case was rejected.

Wanjie Hospital, dissatisfied with the above civil ruling of the original trial court, appealed to this Court, arguing: The original trial court's findings of fact were unclear. In the first loan contract, Zi Zhong Bo Jie Zi No. 2004050, signed between Wanjie Hospital and Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch, the parties explicitly stipulated the method of dispute resolution, i.e., "if negotiation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the Zibo City Arbitration Commission for arbitration." Since the subsequent eight loans were all entered into on the basis of the first loan contract, they should be regarded as a continuation of the first contract. Moreover, the subsequent eight loan contracts were all form contracts. According to the principles of contract interpretation under the Contract Law, an interpretation unfavorable to the party providing the form contract, i.e., Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch, should be adopted. Therefore, for the subsequent eight loan contracts, based on the principle of fairness, the dispute resolution method should be interpreted unfavorable to Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch, i.e., disputes should be submitted to the Zibo City Arbitration Commission for arbitration, which was the true expression of intent of both parties. The original trial court's finding that it had jurisdiction over the subsequent eight contracts constituted an unclear finding of fact. Therefore, Wanjie Hospital requested that the court of second instance revoke the original ruling and dismiss the lawsuit filed by Zhonghang Boshan Sub-branch.

This Court holds: With respect to the nine foreign currency loan contracts entered into by the parties in this case, firstly, the parties did not expressly stipulate or indicate in the contracts the relationship between the nine contracts involved in this case. Secondly, from the content and characteristics of each loan contract, the loan amounts and performance acts were also independent of each other, and no correlation between the contracts can be discerned. Thirdly, from the perspective of contract interpretation, when a dispute arises between the parties over contractual provisions, the intrinsic true expression of intent of the parties must be ascertained. The primary method for determining the true expression of intent of the parties is to ascertain their literal expression of intent. This is the so-called textual interpretation method in contract interpretation. Only when the precise meaning of a provision cannot be determined through textual interpretation may other interpretation methods be used to determine the meaning of the contract provisions and fill gaps in the contract. In this case, except for the first loan contract, the remaining loan contract provisions all clearly state: when a dispute arises, it shall be submitted to the local People's Court for trial. It should be held that this stipulation represents the true intent of the parties. Although the litigation provisions in the relevant loan contracts in this case are clauses in a form contract, they do not, under ordinary understanding, give rise to different interpretations. Therefore, the rules for interpreting standard terms in the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China should not be applied. Wanjie Hospital's appeal ground that the original trial court did not have jurisdiction over the disputes arising from the subsequent eight loan contracts in this case is untenable and is not supported by this Court. The original trial court's finding that, except for the dispute over the loan contract numbered Zi Zhong Bo Jie Zi No. 2004050 for USD 3,000,000 and the corresponding guarantee contract signed on October 14, 2004 (over which the court had no jurisdiction due to the arbitration clause in the contract), the court had jurisdiction over the remaining eight loan contracts in this case is correct and is supported by this Court. Pursuant to Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 8, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs, this Court rules as follows:

The appeal filed by Zibo Wanjie Hospital against the original trial court's ruling on the objection to jurisdiction is dismissed, and the original ruling is affirmed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 50 paid by the appellant, Zibo Wanjie Hospital, for the second instance shall be refunded.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Pei Yingshuo
Judge: Zhu Hainian
Acting Judge: Gong Bangyou

May 25, 2007

Court Clerk: An Yang

Presiding Judge Profile
Pei Yingshuo, Senior Judge: born in 1961, LL.M., served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2001.
